fields.howto_title: How to Write Learning Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write learning and development survey questions for each stage of a program, build the survey, and act on the answers.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match questions to the four levels
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decision the answers will feed, such as which skill gets next year's first workshop or whether a program runs again. Put it in the first line of your prompt. Drop any question that would not change that decision.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about skills before a program starts, about what people learned on the day it ends, and about what they do differently 60 to 90 days later. Give each moment its own short survey instead of one long survey at the end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The Kirkpatrick model breaks evaluation into four levels. Reaction asks whether people found the training engaging, learning whether they acquired the intended knowledge and skills, and behavior whether they perform the new behaviors at work. Write at least one question per level.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent the program, who answers, the questions for each stage, and who reads the results. Emergent turns that description into the survey and a results dashboard. Change any question later by asking for it in one more sentence.
fields.howto_step_5_des: For the follow-up question, write a matching version for each learner's manager, worded about the learner. Asking both sides the same question shows whether a new habit is visible to someone else, not only to the person who took the course.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link to 5 people from the group before launch and have them answer on a phone. Fix any question they read two ways, any rating scale without labels at both ends, and any skill name they never use at work.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the survey closes, pick the lowest score and decide one change. Tell the group in a short note what the answers showed and what happens next. Send that note before the next survey goes out, not after it.

faq_heading: Learning and Development Survey Questions FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 are long lists of training feedback and career development questions (SurveyMonkey, Paycor, AIHR, SmartSurvey), one analytics blog and a Reddit thread, and none says which question belongs at which point of a program. This page sorts learning and development survey questions by the moment they are asked and the decision they feed: a skills check before the training plan, a knowledge check right after a session, a 90-day follow-up that asks the learner and the manager the same question, and a career goals survey that sizes next year's cohorts. Each tab ends in a decision an L&D lead made from the answers, and the how-to maps questions to the four Kirkpatrick levels, sourced to Kirkpatrick Partners.
tab_stories: Thornfield Freight asks its 48 shift supervisors to rate their confidence in 4 skills from 1 to 5 before it sets the year's training plan; 44 answer, coaching averages 2.6 against 3.1 for handling conflict and 4.3 for safety rules, and the first workshop of the year is on coaching.

Tregarth Software sends its 36 account managers 2 ratings and a 5-question knowledge check after a 2-day negotiation training; 34 answer, relevance averages 4.4, and 15 of 34 miss the question on setting a walk-away price, so the trainer adds a role play on it.

Vinterly Home Care asks the 22 graduates of its new-manager program and each graduate's director the same question 90 days later; 20 graduates say they hold a weekly one-on-one with every direct report, directors confirm 13, and the L&D lead gets a Slack message listing the 7 pairs that disagree.

Osterbrook Analytics asks 120 employees which skill they want to grow this year and how they prefer to learn; 96 answer, 38 pick SQL, 52 prefer learning from a colleague, and the first cohort is an 8-week SQL group with peer mentors.

claims_to_source: The Kirkpatrick model breaks evaluation into four levels
The Kirkpatrick model's Level 1 Reaction measures whether the audience finds the training favorable, engaging and relevant
The Kirkpatrick model's Level 2 Learning measures whether the audience acquires the intended knowledge, skills, attitude, confidence and commitment
The Kirkpatrick model's Level 3 Behavior measures whether the audience performs the critical behaviors on the job

chip_adds: Add a skills gap check where staff rate their confidence in each skill from 1 to 5.
Add a 5-question knowledge check that shows how many people missed each question.
Add a 90-day follow-up that asks the learner and their manager the same question.
Add career goals: ask which skill each person wants to grow this year.
